messages:
alex: quick postmortem from this morning's batch-token target sweep — TL;DR: we increased max_tokens_per_batch aggressively to favor throughput, which helped H100/A100 but caused a p99 latency regression on L4 due to KV-fragmentation + kernel fallback.

maria: can you summarize the experiment values and rollout window?

alex: rolled at 03:10 UTC. changes: max_tokens_per_batch set to {H100:120k, A100:80k, A10:60k, L4:32k, T4:36k} and queue policy switched to batch-first (favor fill-to-max) for @low-cost profiles.

sam: perf numbers from the canary pool (5 L4 cards): baseline p99=48ms; after change p99=120ms; p50 stable. throughput improved ~18% overall for mixed workload but 99th latency doubled on L4.

jing: profile traces attached from the runtime sampler (short excerpt):
```
# trace snippet (L4, request len ~2048 tokens)
kernel_select: aten_attention_v1 -> aten_attention_scalar_fallback
kernel_exec: aten_attention_scalar_fallback 90.3ms
kv_merge: fragmentation_rewrite 12.4ms
copy_h2d: 4.1ms
other_kernels: 6.2ms
total_rpc_time: 118.9ms
```

sam: root cause hypothesis: large max_tokens per batch increases KV cache slot fragmentation when mixed early/late position requests interleave. For L4 kernels the fallback path is hit more often (smaller caches + different kernel thresholds), causing O(1) slower attention and more H2D copies.

maria: did we see different kernel selections per card family?

jing: yes — on H100/A100 selector picks tiled_attention_v3 (fast) for long sequences; on L4 selector degrades to scalar fallback for ~22% of batch entries once fragmentation > threshold. The selector metrics show kernel_fallback_count spiked concurrent with the rollout.

alex: important nuance: the batching policy (fill-to-max) was designed to improve throughput but increased intra-batch variance in sequence lengths. That variance amplified KV fragmentation.

sam: reproducer steps I used in canary:
1) send 60 concurrent requests with lengths sampled {32,256,1024,2048} (heavy tail)
2) set max_tokens_per_batch to 32k on L4
3) observe kernel_fallback_count > 20% within 5 minutes

maria: good. what's the proposed mitigation?

alex: propose three changes:
- immediately roll back max_tokens_per_batch for L4 to 24k and T4 to 28k (safety rollback).
- change queue policy for low-memory GPUs to 'variance-aware': prefer grouping by seq_len buckets before filling to max; keep fill-to-max for H100/A100.
- add a KV-frag metric and an escalator that throttles batch expansion when frag > 0.15.

jing: we should also adjust kernel selection thresholds: increase tiled_attention affinity on L4 by relaxing its min_chunk requirement — this reduces fallback. small patch exists in branch `kernel-l4-affinity-tweak`.

sam: numbers from a quick simulator after applying proposed L4 settings: p99 -> 54ms, throughput drop ~3% vs the aggressive setting, but p99 comparable to baseline.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollback for config/max_tokens_per_batch on pool=l4-canary initiated by alex at 03:45 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for l4-canary at 03:50 UTC.

maria: action items:
- alex: roll back L4/T4 global config and put safety cap (done for canary; schedule global rollback if canary stable) — owner alex — due today EOD.
- jing: PR for kernel-l4-affinity-tweak + unit test for selector behavior — owner jing — due +2d.
- sam: write regression test in perf-harness to simulate mixed-length bursts and assert kernel_fallback_count < 5% at target config — owner sam — due +3d.
- eng-telemetry: add KV_frag_ratio metric + alert when >0.10 on any card family — owner maria — due +4d.

alex: proposed new per-GPU conservative targets (post-incident): H100: 120000, A100: 80000, A10: 60000, L4: 24000, T4: 28000. We'll iterate after kernel affinity and queue changes.

maria: also document guidance for customers: prefer 'latency' profile for L4/T4 or set per-request seq_len_hint to let the router bucket requests. I'll draft a short note for the docs site.

sam: one more note: KV cache compaction runs are expensive; we should consider incremental compaction during low-util intervals rather than on-demand during high throughput. Filing follow-up ticket.

jing: re: tests — I'll include kernel selector traces in the CI artifact so we can catch fallbacks in future.

alex: thanks all. overall: revert aggressive global max_tokens_per_batch for L4/T4, enable variance-aware queueing on low-memory card families, tweak kernel affinity for L4, add KV frag metric. will wait 24h on canary before wider rollout. :thumbsup:

maria: noted. :thumbsup:

sam: ack.

jing: ack.

(attachments: links to perf graphs and traces -> https://perf.redwood.internal/graphs/6043219876 and https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/6043219876)
